Both sources have valid SHA-256 checksums provided, ensuring integrity verification during package build. There are no signs of obfuscated URLs, suspicious network requests, or execution of downloaded content outside standard packaging procedures.

The package depends only on `python` and build-time dependencies (`python-build`, `python-installer`, `python-setuptools`), which are typical for Python packages. The inclusion of a patch from a GitHub PR commit is not inherently unsafe—it is a common practice to apply fixes not yet included in an upstream release. Since the patch source is a specific, immutable commit hash and its checksum is verified, the risk of tampering is minimal. No dangerous operations such as unchecked runtime downloads, use of `eval`, or file exfiltration are present in this metadata file.

This file contains only declarative packaging metadata and no executable code. All actions it implies (downloading versioned source, applying a checksummed patch, building with standard Python tooling) are consistent with safe AUR packaging practices. The use of `any` architecture and `!emptydirs` option is normal for pure Python packages. No red flags indicating supply chain attacks or malicious behavior were found.
</details>
